analysis:
The change is documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md is a modified 100644 file, and I saw only head text with no patch or base text, so I could not tell which lines changed. The text describes provider CLI behavior that is stated to be unchanged or fail-closed, and adds no new code, endpoint, or trust path. Reviewed claims:
- cache: the daily write limit and directory selection never migrate or format disks, and invalid or changed storage disables the SSD cache. This is consistent with T-041; the CLI reference does not change the posture.
- enroll: on macOS 27 and later it gives App Attest guidance only. The text says it is not a grant and that the OS choice never grants serving authorization or removes a profile. This is consistent with T-052/T-036/TB-011.
- unenroll --keep-serving: requires fresh coordinator App Attest removal readiness (T-057).
- switch and restart: they require coordinator receipts, drain, and fresh authorization (T-053).
- stop: drains before stopping and does not silently SIGKILL.
- autopilot: shadow by default, with consent not equal to activation.
- local mode: --no-auth and --bind are documented as trusted-only, which is pre-existing.
No security regression, new attack surface, or invalidated threat assumption is introduced by the visible text. Residual limit: no diff was supplied, so I could not confirm which statements are new. The documented behavior matches the canonical context, but I did not verify it against the unchanged Swift/Go source that the doc cites.
